traps: 📄 Built from the LECTURE TRANSCRIPT only (Dr. Diehl, Mon 11/2). Slides not uploaded yet — slides win any disagreement; slide numbers get added when the deck arrives.
✏️ CORRECTED in lecture: GENIOGLOSSUS action = PROTRUSION of the tongue (cross out the slide's action).
✏️ Slide error: 'glossa' is GREEK (lingua = Latin). She doesn't care which language — know the MEANINGS.
Vestibule = OUTSIDE the teeth (rostral + lateral) · Oral cavity proper = INSIDE the teeth (tongue's space).
LABIAL vestibule = lips ↔ incisors (rostral) · BUCCAL vestibule = cheeks ↔ teeth (lateral).
PALATOPHARYNGEAL arch = palate → pharynx (forms the intrapharyngeal opening; find in lab) · PALATOGLOSSAL arch = palate → tongue.
CHOANAE = caudal openings of the nasal cavity · CONCHAE = bony scrolls inside the nasal cavity.
Soft palate: ORAL mucosa ventrally (faces the mouth) · RESPIRATORY mucosa dorsally (faces the nasopharynx).
FILIFORM papillae = NO taste (mechanical only). The other three (fungiform, foliate, vallate) are the taste-bearing ones.
Vallate = circumvallate (same papillae) — the V at the root of the tongue.
HYOglossus (muscle) vs HYPOglossal (nerve, CN XII): the nerve runs LATERAL on the muscle; the lingual a. is MEDIAL (deep).
Lingual a. = external carotid branch · SUBlingual a. = FACIAL a. branch (facial = external carotid branch).
Tongue nerves: lingual n. = general sensation rostral 2/3 · chorda tympani = TASTE rostral 2/3 · glossopharyngeal (IX) = taste caudal 1/3 · hypoglossal (XII) = the ONLY motor.
Parotid duct AND zygomatic duct → BUCCAL vestibule (zygomatic ~1 cm caudal) · Mandibular duct → SUBLINGUAL CARUNCLE.
Arteries BRANCH, veins MERGE — say venous names in drainage order.

⚠️ FLAG — monostomatic vs polystomatic: lecture paired 'major = monostomatic (one duct)' and 'minor = polystomatic (many ducts)' while describing the sublingual gland, which has both parts. Safe answer: monostomatic = one duct, polystomatic = many ducts. Check the slide wording.

⚠️ FLAG — linguofacial vein: lecture once says facial + SUBlingual meet to form it, then summarizes facial + LINGUAL. Use facial + lingual = linguofacial (sublingual drains into lingual). Confirm on the slide.
